The new violations involved additional recordkeeping failures that occurred after the 2019 order. Specifically, beginning in March 2020, hardware failures connected to a vendor service, exacerbated by increased usage during the COVID-19 pandemic, resulted in Goldman failing to record and retain thousands of calls made on mobile devices. [3, 4] While financial terms were not disclosed, Goldman Sachs stated the transaction would result in a gain. metadata.original_text: This time series records goldman sachs data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-12-21 to 2026-03-08. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On December 11, 2025, Harness, an AI software delivery platform, announced it had raised a $240 million Series E financing round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The funding will be used to accelerate the company's platform innovation and drive its global expansion. <2> On December 1, 2025, Goldman Sachs announced a $2 billion agreement to acquire Innovator Capital Management. Innovator is recognized as an industry pioneer in defined outcome, or 'buffer,' ETFs, managing $28 billion in assets under supervision across 159 funds as of September 30, 2025. The strategic acquisition aims to significantly expand Goldman Sachs Asset Management's active ETF capabilities and custom portfolio solutions, instantly vaulting its total ETF assets from $51 billion to $79 billion and positioning the firm among the top 10 largest active ETF issuers. <3> Goldman Sachs has raised its copper price forecast for December 2025 to $10,610 per metric ton, driven by an expected supply deficit later in the decade. The bank cited growing demand from key sectors like renewable energy and electric vehicles, coupled with supply shortages caused by delayed mining projects being put on hold. Additionally, Goldman Sachs maintained its long-term price range estimate of $10,000 to $11,000 per ton for the period spanning 2026 to 2027. <4> San Francisco-based Federato, an AI-native insurance software platform, announced it has raised $100 million in a Series D funding round led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. <5> Goldman Sachs Research published a comprehensive analysis predicting that U.S. equities, specifically the S&P 500, will underperform international markets over the next decade due to elevated valuations. Led by David Kostin, the equity strategy team forecasts a modest 3% annualized nominal total return for the S&P 500 through 2034. Broader U.S. equities are expected to yield annualized returns of 6.5%, significantly lagging behind the 10.9% forecast for Emerging Markets and 10.3% for Asia ex-Japan. A primary driver of this cautious outlook is the current cyclically adjusted price-earnings (CAPE) ratio of 38, which stands in the 97th historical percentile, indicating that high starting valuations will likely constrain future growth. <6> On November 10, 2025, Goldman Sachs Alternatives entered into a definitive agreement to form a strategic partnership with New York-based Excel Sports Management. Through an investment of approximately $1 billion, Goldman Sachs takes a controlling stake in the talent agency. The partnership is aimed at accelerating Excel's global expansion, integrating services, and creating new revenue verticals by leveraging Goldman's extensive resources and expertise. <7> On December 9, 2025, Goldman Sachs hosted its U.S. Financial Services Conference in New York, which featured a prominent scheduled address by the firm's Chief Financial Officer, Denis Coleman. The speaking engagement was officially announced by the firm on November 10, 2025. <8> Goldman Sachs announced its third-quarter 2025 financial results on October 14, 2025, beating market expectations. The company reported a 20% year-over-year increase in net revenues to $15.18 billion. Net earnings saw a significant 37% surge to $4.10 billion, resulting in diluted earnings per common share of $12.25. <9> Marcus by Goldman Sachs released its September 2025 market recap, noting that despite September's reputation as a weak month for equities, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted strong returns of 3.7% and 5.7%, respectively. This performance marked the best September for both indices in 15 years, a rally driven by the Federal Reserve's decision to cut its policy rate, strong US economic activity, and an investor frenzy around artificial intelligence. The report also highlighted stronger-than-expected economic growth, with the third estimate for second-quarter 2025 GDP revised up to a 3.8% annual rate, a significant rebound from the 0.6% contraction in the first quarter. This strength contrasted with a weakening labor market, as job gains slowed significantly in August, with some data suggesting a continued slowdown in employment growth into September. <10> David Solomon, Chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs, is scheduled to speak at the Barclays 23rd Annual Global Financial Services Conference on Monday, September 8, 2025, at 4:15 pm (ET). The initial announcement of his scheduled appearance was published on August 4, 2025.
